key_insight: WorldWeaver (W^2) introduces cross-agent world state registers so a diffusion model can keep a shared, persistent state while generating observations over time. This helps multi-agent and multi-view rollouts stay consistent beyond short-lived observation history.
problem_solved: Existing autoregressive video diffusion models mainly pass along past observations as context, which makes it hard to preserve a common world state across multiple agents and viewpoints. The result is inconsistent long-horizon behavior when agents interact or when views change.
method: Uses a streaming multi-agent autoregressive diffusion setup for rollout generation.
Adds world state registers to carry shared latent state across agents and across views.
Decouples persistent world state from raw observation history to improve consistency during generation.
impact: This is useful for building interactive simulators, embodied AI systems, and multi-agent world models that need coherent long-term memory. For practitioners, it offers a more scalable way to generate synchronized multi-agent scenes without relying only on observation conditioning.
